## Measured summary

Actual official JSON rows: **1120**; distinct IDs: **1094**; loaded per-category Map rows: **1119**; distinct duplicate IDs: **25**. The index declares 1,110 rows (S:public/data/equipment/official/index.json:47), while its weapon total omits the nine physical rows and its miscellaneous count misses a duplicate Cargo. Runtime insertion/lookup rules: S:src/services/equipment/EquipmentOfficialLoader.ts:129; S:src/services/equipment/EquipmentLoaderService.ts:139. Detailed evidence is in the duplicate and per-file tables below.

Numeric-zero-damage weapon rows: **280**; ammo rows with empty compatibility: **237**; explicitly variable rows without a matching service formula: **64**. These are selectors requiring semantic review, not counts of proven unsupported equipment. The actual source-backed matrices distinguish implemented special effects and excluded unit types (S:src/simulation/runner/CombatFeatureSupport.specialWeaponFamilies.ts:46; S:src/simulation/runner/CombatAmmunitionSupport.ts:189).

Source inventory: **1902 explicit base registrations/factory recipes**. This is not a complete Java runtime total: generated munition mutations and SmallWeaponAmmoType are separate below (M:src/megamek/common/equipment/EquipmentType.java:767; M:src/megamek/common/equipment/SmallWeaponAmmoType.java:89).

## Highest-priority findings

1. **Repair source identity and aliases before adding more rows.** The three lookup paths disagree, 441 JSON mapping keys reference 83 targets absent as direct equipment IDs, and 25 static MTF mapper keys point at missing direct IDs. A mapper can report success before proving its target exists. See sections 1.1-1.3 and their cited rows (S:src/services/equipment/EquipmentNameMapper.ts:242; S:src/utils/construction/equipmentBV/normalization.ts:32).
2. **Repair existing quirk semantics.** The imported corpus contains raw MegaMek IDs such as imp_target_short and easy_pilot, while local helpers use different IDs and hydration passes through unchanged. The present importer also loses weapon-quirk assignment data at the canonical JSON boundary: 0 of 4,225 design files contain a top-level weaponQuirks object. See the actual file census in section 7 (S:scripts/megameklab-conversion/mtf_parser.py:248; S:src/simulation/runner/UnitHydrationMovement.ts:338; S:src/utils/gameplay/quirkModifiers/targetingQuirks.ts:23).
3. **Repair damage and metadata with a bounded source-proven cohort.** HAG/20 is marked UNOFFICIAL with damage 0 in the JSON, but the source explicitly sets unofficial=false and static tech STANDARD. The extractor's substring heuristic can misread setUnofficial(false); runtime then maps UNOFFICIAL to Experimental. Positive BV alone does not make this a working weapon (S:public/data/equipment/official/weapons/ballistic-other.json:279; M:src/megamek/common/weapons/gaussRifles/clan/CLHAG20.java:80; M:src/megamek/common/weapons/gaussRifles/clan/CLHAG20.java:87; S:scripts/extract-megamek-equipment.js:67; S:src/services/units/EnumParserRegistry.ts:178).
4. **Keep bounded support credited.** The canonical SPA matrix has 46 integrated and 45 out-of-scope rows; the local quirk matrix has 26 integrated and 5 out-of-scope rows. The source registration comparison finds 94 unique unit quirk options, 17 weapon quirk options, and 92 pilot option IDs; the extra pilot ID absent from the 91-SPA catalog is the numeric edge field, not an omitted ability. Full rows and defining citations appear in section 4 (M:src/megamek/common/options/PilotOptions.java:124; S:src/lib/spa/canonicalCatalog.ts:1; S:src/simulation/runner/CombatCanonicalSpaSupport.catalog.ts:147).
5. **Treat full equipment/universe acquisition as NEW backlog.** Existing U79-U82 own the unit catalog, and P7 owns pilot authority/travel/opportunities while excluding automatic catalog expansion. Sections 9-10 map every gap group and rank lanes with file ownership/dependencies and L1 collision status (S:openspec/planning/2026-09-12-roadmap-completion/units.json:15799; P:PLAN.md:127; P:PLAN.md:133).

The detailed inventory is intentionally exhaustive. For decisions, read this section, section 9's ownership crosswalk and section 10's ranked lanes first; sections 1-8 provide the cited denominators and individual records.

## 1. Equipment census

Every items[] row in the index-named files was counted directly, including ignored generated JSON. The registry probe reproduces index-order Map insertion with the actual converter functions, then calls EquipmentRegistry.initialize with network loading stubbed as already loaded. It uses converted TechBase enums, not raw CLAN/INNER_SPHERE strings (S:src/services/equipment/EquipmentConverters.ts:114; S:src/services/equipment/EquipmentRegistry.ts:148). BV/combat probes call the real pure catalog and lookup functions; no test runner or app startup is involved.

The Registry, BV normalizer and combat lookup are separate contracts. The registry builds aliases, BV reads name-mappings plus normalization patterns, and combat adds source-backed aliases and can remove tech prefixes. Retain source tech/internal name and review wrong-tech/wrong-category hits, including alias collisions (S:src/services/equipment/EquipmentRegistry.ts:227; S:src/utils/construction/equipmentBV/normalization.ts:91; S:src/simulation/runner/UnitHydrationCatalogLookup.ts:155).

Armor belongs to separate type-specific construction definitions, not EquipmentRegistry. MekStation has 10 BattleMech ARMOR_DEFINITIONS; do not call all 67 MegaMek armor recipes absent on the strength of Registry misses alone (S:src/types/construction/ArmorType.ts:15; S:src/types/construction/ArmorType.ts:51; M:src/megamek/common/equipment/ArmorType.java:113).

## 2. Full explicit MegaMek base inventory

Method: strip comments; enumerate active no-argument constructor registrations in WeaponType.initializeTypes and unique zero-argument factory calls in the AmmoType/MiscType/ArmorType/BombType initializers; follow constructor inheritance and literal/static String names, BombTypeEnum and structure-name getters. Uncalled factories are excluded. This counts recipes, not distinct runtime internal names. The defining source is cited in each row.

Registry = converted EquipmentRegistry result; BV = resolved canonical ID/value, or UNRESOLVED (= resolved:false); Combat = weapon/ammo lookup only, never a claim that all its mechanics work. D0 = numeric zero damage. Other candidates are obtained from source display/lookup names and are not accepted equivalents. All gaps in this section map to G1/G2/G3 in the ownership crosswalk; armor requires its separate subsystem comparison.

## 3. Data exists but requires semantic treatment

### 3.1 Duplicate IDs

Weapons win over ammo/electronics/misc in EquipmentLoaderService.getById. BV loads weapons first and avoids overwriting existing IDs with other categories, except rows skipped for missing fields; physical formulas therefore require separate care (S:src/services/equipment/EquipmentLoaderService.ts:139; S:src/utils/construction/equipmentBV/catalogLoader.ts:109). ### 3.2 All numeric-zero-damage weapons (280)

Numeric zero passes unchanged through resolveCatalogDamage; missile strings have a separate parser. AMS/NARC/plasma can legitimately have zero conventional damage because dedicated handlers exist. Thus this is not 280 proven missing implementations. Streak/HAG and excluded artillery/torpedo/infantry families require source-backed damage/handler/scope review (S:src/simulation/runner/UnitHydrationWeapons.ts:26; S:src/simulation/runner/CombatFeatureSupport.specialWeaponFamilies.ts:63). G3 applies.

Historical extractor mechanism: default damage 0 and literal-only damage regex, without Java superclass/sentinel interpretation; this does not prove every current row came from a particular invocation (S:scripts/extract-megamek-equipment.js:144; S:scripts/extract-megamek-equipment.js:194).

## 5. MegaMek-generated ammunition

The section 2 source count includes base recipes only. AmmoType.initializeTypes builds mutation lists and calls createMunitions; internal names/lookup aliases are transformed differently per ammo family (M:src/megamek/common/equipment/AmmoType.java:3501; M:src/megamek/common/equipment/AmmoType.java:15580). SmallWeaponAmmoType separately creates ammo for every eligible registered InfantryWeapon, stripping Inferno and appending ` Ammo` (M:src/megamek/common/equipment/SmallWeaponAmmoType.java:51; M:src/megamek/common/equipment/SmallWeaponAmmoType.java:71; M:src/megamek/common/equipment/SmallWeaponAmmoType.java:89). A future source-pinned export must include these generated aliases and flags; the report makes no invented full runtime total. G1/G3 apply.

## 6. Optional rules: TacOps / IO / aerospace / StratOps discovery

MekStation already carries optionalRules in session and command state and implements specific switches. Its support maps are not a universal GameOptions mirror (S:src/types/gameplay/GameSessionUnitTypes.ts:36; S:src/types/gameplay/TacticalCommandInterfaces.ts:254; S:src/simulation/runner/CombatRuleSupport.ts:1). Examples include TacOps LOS1 and PLAYTEST_3 AMS reuse (S:src/simulation/runner/CombatRuleSupport.terrainLos.ts:169; S:src/simulation/runner/CombatSpecialWeaponSupport.ams.ts:89).

The following inventory selects active GameOptions.addOption registrations whose constants contain TAC_OPS/STRATOPS/INTERSTELLAR or belong to advAeroRules. It searches product .ts/.tsx source for the case-insensitive constant name OR exact quoted option ID, excluding tests/stories/support/source-reference catalogs and comments. A hit is discovery evidence only; a miss does not prove no differently named helper exists. IO has no dedicated INTERSTELLAR constant family in the inspected GameOptions source; IO equipment/armor/bioware also needs rulesRefs and per-type scope analysis (M:src/megamek/common/options/GameOptions.java:268; M:src/megamek/common/equipment/ArmorType.java:994; S:src/simulation/runner/CombatCanonicalSpaSupport.catalog.ts:98). Every residual here maps to G6 in section 9.

Parameterized obsolete:year must retain the parameter rather than becoming an unqualified boolean.

The inspected MekStation loaders do not import the full unified faction/command history, upstream era XML, planetary time/event/orbital/socioeconomic history, text RAT collections, forcegenerator availability, MekHQ RAT metadata, or personnel SPA acquisition policy. This is bounded to source/catalogs in this worktree, not inaccessible branches. The concrete local alternatives are the compiled TS tables and 3025 seed above. Its mm-data integration fetches record-sheet assets, as established in the prior loader report (S:config/mm-data-assets.json:2; S:scripts/mm-data/fetch-assets.ts:39). G5 covers SPA policy; G7 factions/eras; G8 RATs; G9 planetary systems.

MegaMek Factions2 loads internal YAML factions and commands then user overrides; MekHQ Factions delegates to it (M:src/megamek/common/universe/Factions2.java:160; H:src/mekhq/campaign/universe/Factions.java:208). MegaMek Eras parses eras.xml safely (M:src/megamek/common/eras/Eras.java:233). MekHQ Systems recursively reads YAML and user overrides; stale XML comments there do not change the file format (H:src/mekhq/campaign/universe/Systems.java:239; H:src/mekhq/campaign/universe/Systems.java:295).

There are three distinct RAT surfaces: textual unit/weight tables, numeric-era chassis/model/faction availability, and MekHQ collection metadata. RandomUnitGenerator recursively loads army tables and resolves against MekSummaryCache; RATGenerator loads bracketing era files and filters unified factions for rating systems; RATManager consumes collection metadata and waits for the text generator for validation (M:src/megamek/client/generator/RandomUnitGenerator.java:272; M:src/megamek/client/ratgenerator/RATGenerator.java:1408; M:src/megamek/client/ratgenerator/RATGenerator.java:1425; M:src/megamek/client/ratgenerator/RATGenerator.java:1450; H:src/mekhq/campaign/universe/RATManager.java:141). A data importer must preserve these separate meanings.

MekStation getRAT tries faction:era, then any same-faction table, then Pirates. Its separate seeded inverse-BV/chassis-cap force generator is implemented, but neither path is MegaMek availability parity (S:src/constants/scenario/rats/ratRegistry.ts:24; S:src/services/encounter/randomForceGenerator.ts:1; S:src/services/encounter/randomForceGenerator.ts:32).

### 8.4 Quirk source caution

Quirk definitions are Java options and unit assignments are MTF/BLK QuirkEntry data validated on Entity/Mounted. This MegaMek checkout has no mmconf/canonUnitQuirks.xml; QuirksPanel retains a historical XML comment. MekHQ has mmconf/defaultQuirks.xml but no current src Java reference to that filename was found. Do not treat either the stale comment or that MekHQ XML as an active MegaMek loader contract (M:src/megamek/common/options/Quirks.java:62; M:src/megamek/common/options/WeaponQuirks.java:59; M:src/megamek/common/loaders/BLKFile.java:172; M:src/megamek/common/loaders/MtfFile.java:542; M:src/megamek/common/units/Entity.java:14464; M:src/megamek/client/ui/dialogs/customMek/QuirksPanel.java:77; H:mmconf/defaultQuirks.xml:3).

### 9.1 Concrete construction and behavior boundaries

- **BattleMech/vehicle armor:** shared ARMOR_DEFINITIONS has 10 entries and vehicle armor consumes it. It lacks constructor choices for Heat-Dissipating, Impact-Resistant, Anti-Penetrative Ablation, Ballistic-Reinforced, primitive/industrial/commercial and support BAR families present in MegaMek's 67 armor recipes. Some may have serialized identifiers or bounded runtime behavior elsewhere; this is a concrete construction-definition gap, not a claim of universal absence (S:src/types/construction/ArmorType.ts:15; S:src/types/construction/ArmorType.ts:51; S:src/utils/construction/vehicle/armor.ts:62; M:src/megamek/common/equipment/ArmorType.java:994; M:src/megamek/common/equipment/ArmorType.java:1021; M:src/megamek/common/equipment/ArmorType.java:1045; M:src/megamek/common/equipment/ArmorType.java:1073).
- **Other armor models must stay separate:** BA construction has 8 armor enum/data entries, including stealth/mimetic/reactive/reflective/fire-resistant; ProtoMech's unit interface accepts only Standard. The aerospace BV adapter accepts string keys but defaults numeric/absent inputs, which does not establish full aerospace armor construction or typed import. G2 owns the new armor parity backlog (S:src/types/unit/BattleArmorInterfaces.ts:167; S:src/types/unit/BattleArmorInterfaces.ts:196; S:src/types/unit/ProtoMechInterfaces.ts:206; S:src/utils/construction/aerospace/aerospaceBVUnitAdapter.ts:43).
- **TSEMP and BattleMech Taser** have data, numeric damage 0, and no dedicated effect resolution found in the inspected engine/gameplay/runner product sources; this is a source-search finding, not an executed failing scenario. **HAG/20,30,40** also have zero damage in the present catalog; no dedicated HAG handler was found in those paths. Scope these as G3 after source-backed effect/damage acceptance is written (S:public/data/equipment/official/weapons/energy-other.json:29; S:public/data/equipment/official/weapons/ballistic-other.json:279; S:src/simulation/runner/UnitHydrationWeapons.ts:26).
- **Streak:** the local support matrix expressly integrates damage-capable Streak SRM and keeps zero-damage Streak LRM/OS/prototypes as data gaps; six ordinary IS/Clan Streak SRM IDs are not the same scope as all source Streak registrations. The exact zero-data IDs are pinned in the test source, which was read rather than run (S:src/simulation/runner/CombatFeatureSupport.specialWeaponFamilies.ts:63; S:src/simulation/runner/**tests**/battlemechCombatCatalog.test-helpers.ts:607; S:src/simulation/runner/**tests**/battlemechCombatCatalog.test-helpers.ts:616).
- **Bombs/artillery:** section 2 lists all 18 registered BombType recipes and their internal names; none resolves in the equipment/BV catalogs probed here. Bombing/scatter and artillery effects need their own flow, not generic direct-fire damage. The canonical Golden Goose and Oblique Artilleryman rows explicitly exclude those matrices, while indirect fire and Oblique Attacker have narrower implemented behavior (M:src/megamek/common/equipment/enums/BombType.java:261; S:src/simulation/runner/CombatCanonicalSpaSupport.entries.ts:47; S:src/simulation/runner/CombatCanonicalSpaSupport.entries.ts:59; S:src/simulation/runner/CombatAmmunitionSupport.ts:244).
- **Metadata extraction needs repair before expansion:** the historical extractor matches numeric literal assignments and text fragments rather than evaluating inherited Java constructors or date-specific rules availability. Its -UNOFFICIAL" substring heuristic can match a setUnofficial(false) call; current JSON metadata must be checked against source, not treated as authority. The missing-equipment helper also reads old weapons/energy.json, electronics.json etc. paths. Do not run these writers against the present catalogs without repairing their input/output contract (S:scripts/extract-megamek-equipment.js:67; S:scripts/extract-megamek-equipment.js:194; S:scripts/extract-missing-equipment.js:45).
- **Fail-closed seams exist:** strict weapon hydration rejects unresolved IDs and units without combat weapons. Generic hydration also has a non-strict wrapper. The report does not equate a catalog presence/lookup hit with a successful strict runtime path (S:src/simulation/runner/UnitHydrationWeapons.ts:272; S:src/simulation/runner/UnitHydrationWeapons.ts:303).

### 9.2 Verification limits and reproducibility

Reference HEADs observed read-only: MegaMek `325b2504c7b7750ecdcb85468621fb2de2ad8e60`, mm-data `b67baa5ecc765435425fd8cb703a6da909478b7a`, MekHQ `a5fe1b2e227b900cb8576b4b3082c45b03a31edc`. HEADs do not certify clean reference worktrees; no reference file was changed. The research worktree remained clean. The report's source enumeration is an auditable static base-recipe inventory, not Java runtime export or a legal/rules oracle.

Reproduce the count method without builds: enumerate the index's files and sum actual items[]; retain duplicates rather than using its totalItems metadata. Apply the actual TS converter functions and index-order category Maps before invoking EquipmentRegistry. Invoke the pure BV normalization/resolution and catalog weapon/ammo lookup functions against those same checked-out files. Enumerate source initializer registrations with comments removed; follow no-argument superclass constructors and named factory bodies for internal names and explicit TechBase. Keep generated ammo, source recipes, unique internal names and alias keys as different denominators. This report does not claim exact dynamic munition expansion totals; a future isolated exporter is the missing evidence (S:src/services/equipment/EquipmentOfficialLoader.ts:97; S:src/services/equipment/EquipmentConverters.ts:114; M:src/megamek/common/equipment/EquipmentType.java:762).

For derived data, retain source commit/path/hash, original internal name, aliases, unit applicability, tech/date information, mounting/size parameters and upstream notices. mm-data's files carry CC BY-NC-SA attribution; MegaMek Java source is GPL, so copying code is a separate decision from extracting attributed data (D:README.md:16; D:data/universe/factions/FS.yml:1; M:src/megamek/common/equipment/AmmoType.java:11). No assets or source code were imported by this research.

The in-memory scripts loaded pure TS modules through TypeScript transpilation only; this was not a typecheck or application build. Registry acquisition was stubbed, never fetched. Tests cited above are source evidence only. Runtime acceptance should use held-out source records and distinguish alias resolution, construction legality, BV contribution, combat effects, ammo lifecycle, persistence/replay and UI authoring.

## 10. Ranked recommended lanes

All lanes below are recommendations, not admitted product units. **Read-only preparation can run now in parallel with L1.** PLAN.md requires one product-writing task at a time; "no L1 path collision" therefore does not waive the delivery cadence (P:PLAN.md:162). L1's current path is identified in P:PLAN.md:21, and U38 owns server/campaign unit authority (S:openspec/planning/2026-09-12-roadmap-completion/units.json:10380).

File ownership: proposed new `scripts/research/equipment-coverage` and `docs/audits` first; later exact admissions for `src/services/equipment/aliases`, `src/utils/construction/equipmentBV` and catalog generators. Dependencies: pinned upstream source/data and a reviewed matching contract; coordinate `scripts/megameklab-conversion` with U79. **Parallel with L1 now: yes for read-only preparation and isolated manifest design; proposed source paths avoid every named L1 path.** Product edits still need a NEW bounded backlog unit; do not hand-edit generated JSON. File ownership: proposed pure alias/adapter module under `src/services/conversion` or `src/utils/gameplay/quirkModifiers` plus narrowly scoped importer tests; Python parser/output changes coordinate with U79. Dependencies: lane 1 identity contract; source-backed case fixtures including targeting/piloting/actuator aliases and mount-qualified weapon quirks. **Parallel with L1 now: yes for read-only preparation; pure converter/helper scope avoids L1.** Persisted co-op/campaign projections are excluded from this lane and require their authority owners (S:src/simulation/runner/UnitHydrationMovement.ts:338; S:scripts/megameklab-conversion/mtf_parser.py:248; S:openspec/planning/2026-09-12-roadmap-completion/units.json:15799).
